pins.function: 3V3_EN: the SMPS enable pin; shorting it low turns the 3.3 V supply off

pins.name: VSYS
pins.function: VSYS: the system input, 1.8 V to 5.5 V; on USB it is VBUS less a Schottky diode drop

electrical.supply_current_note: The Pico datasheet recommends keeping the load on the 3V3(OUT) pin under 300 mA.
electrical.supply_current_basis: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet, section 2.1: recommended load on 3V3(OUT) less than 300 mA
electrical.supply_current_practice: General practice, not from the datasheet: a weak charger, a long or thin cable, or an unpowered hub may not deliver what the board draws; the usual symptom is a reset or a USB dropout.
electrical.datasheet_basis: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet; RP2040 datasheet
electrical.header_types_basis: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet, section 2.1 and Figure 2 (pinout)
electrical.input_high_note: The RP2040 datasheet lists the maximum voltage at an I/O pin as IOVDD + 0.5 V.
electrical.input_high_basis: RP2040 datasheet, 5.5.3.1 Absolute Maximum Ratings: VPIN max is IOVDD + 0.5 V
electrical.i2c_defaults_basis: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet, Figure 2: I2C0 SDA on GP4 and I2C0 SCL on GP5 are marked as the default I2C pins
electrical.i2c_remap_note: The RP2040 moves each I2C controller only to the pins marked for it in the pinout, and your code must name the pins.
electrical.i2c_pin_note: I2C0 SDA is on GP0, GP4, GP8, GP12, GP16 or GP20 and its SCL on GP1, GP5, GP9, GP13, GP17 or GP21; I2C1 SDA is on GP2, GP6, GP10, GP14, GP18 or GP26 and its SCL on GP3, GP7, GP11, GP15, GP19 or GP27.
electrical.supply_options_note: Power a Pico from Micro-USB, or from VSYS (about 1.8 V to 5.5 V) when USB is not used. A second source must reach VSYS through a diode or a P-channel MOSFET so it cannot feed back into USB. General practice, not from the datasheet: 3V3(OUT) is an output, so nothing else should drive it.
electrical.supply_options_basis: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet, 4.5 Powering Pico
electrical.supply_check_step: Power the Pico from USB alone. A second supply needs a diode or a P-channel MOSFET into VSYS (datasheet section 4.5); do not wire one to 3V3(OUT).
electrical.supply_power_step: Power the Pico from Micro-USB alone: no second supply on VSYS or 3V3(OUT).

dimension_basis.pcb: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet Figure 3, unit mm: 21 x 51, 1 mm thick, rows 17.78 apart, 2.54 pitch, 48.26 between the first and last pin; the first pin's inset from the end is taken as (51 - 48.26) / 2 = 1.37 mm and the drawing shows it to about 0.2 mm
dimension_basis.usb: measured off the same drawing, plus or minus 0.3 mm: 8 mm wide, centred, overhanging the top edge by about 1.4 mm; height is typical for a Micro-USB receptacle (not on the drawing)
dimension_basis.heights: the 3.0 mm above the board and the 6.0 mm of header below it are typical for a board on standard 2.54 mm headers, not on the drawing: measure yours

sources.label: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet (pinout Figure 2, dimensions Figure 3, power chain section 4, power consumption section 3)
RP2040 datasheet (absolute maximum ratings, I2C pin functions)

notes: GPIO23, GPIO24, GPIO25 and GPIO29 are used on the board and are not on the headers.
GP26, GP27 and GP28 can be analogue inputs; their pins have a diode to the 3.3 V rail, so the input must not exceed IOVDD plus about 300 mV.
Only the pins marked I2C0 or I2C1 in the pinout can carry that I2C controller's SDA or SCL.

operating_temp_c.locator: Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet, 2.3 Recommended operating conditions: recommended maximum ambient temperature of operation is 70 C (85 C including self-heating), minimum -20 C

loads.conditions: 25 C mean of three boards; includes the VGA, SD card and I2S audio board attached, so it overstates a bare Pico

loads.mode: Popcorn demo, maximum VBUS current, power saving disabled
loads.conditions: mean of three boards at 25 C and 85 C; includes the VGA board

power_stage.note: an RT6150 buck-boost converter makes the 3.3 V from VSYS

gaps.reason: The Pico datasheet gives example VBUS currents but no minimum supply current.
